name: Avinashilingeswarar Temple, Avinashi (Thiruppukkoliyur)
deity: Shiva as Avinashilingeswarar (Avinashiappar), with the goddess Karunambigai
period: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of Kongu Nadu, sung by Sundarar in the Tevaram (8th century)
dynasty: Chola, Pandya and Hoysala endowments, with later additions
summary: At Avinashi — the Thiruppukkoliyur of the Tevaram — Shiva is the Imperishable Lord, and the lotus tank nearby remembers the day Sundarar sang a lost child back from the jaws of a crocodile.

sections.history: Avinashi stands on the old highway between Coimbatore and Erode in Tiruppur district, and its great Shiva temple is the Thiruppukkoliyur of the Tevaram. It is one of the 276 Paadal Petra Sthalams, a Paadal Petra Sthalam of Kongu Nadu, and the temple's own tradition counts it first among the seven Tevaram shrines of the Kongu country. Sundarar sang the Lord here. Inscriptions on its walls speak of the town as Dakshina Varanasi, the Kashi of the south, and record gifts from the Cholas, the Pandyas and the Hoysalas — a sign of how many dynasties honoured this crossroads shrine of the western Tamil country.
sections.architecture: The temple is a large Dravidian complex, with the main sanctum of Avinashilingeswarar and a separate shrine for the goddess Karunambigai, so revered that the temple is sometimes called after her. Among its sacred waters is the Kasi Kinaru, a well that ties the shrine to its title of southern Kashi. Half a kilometre away lies the Thamarai Kulam, the lotus tank, with a small shrine to Sundarar on its bank and a sculpture of a great crocodile with a boy emerging from its mouth.
sections.legends: Passing through Avinashi, Sundarar heard music from one house and weeping from the house opposite. In the first, a boy was receiving the sacred thread; in the second, parents mourned a son of the same age, seized years before by a crocodile in the lotus tank. Moved, Sundarar went to the tank and sang a pathigam to the Lord of Thiruppukkoliyur. Tradition says the crocodile gave back the child — not as he had been, but grown to the age he would have reached, ready for his own thread ceremony.
sections.festivals: The great festival is the Chithirai brahmotsavam in April–May, crowned by the procession of the temple car — one of the largest and most finely carved in South India, rebuilt after the old car was lost to fire. The crocodile miracle is remembered at the lotus tank around Panguni Uthiram; confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Come for the darshan of the Imperishable Lord and of Karunambigai, then walk to the Thamarai Kulam to see the crocodile and the child in stone and pause at Sundarar's shrine. Tradition says the temple's pathiri tree flowers only at brahmotsavam time. Thirumuruganpoondi, another Sundarar shrine, is a short drive towards Tiruppur.

visit.timings: Open daily in morning and evening sessions with a midday closure, as at most Kongu Nadu temples; hours are extended on festival days. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left outside before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted inside the sanctum; in the outer areas, ask the temple staff before taking pictures, especially of rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Avinashi lies on the Salem–Coimbatore highway (NH 544), about 13 km north of Tiruppur and roughly 40 km north-east of Coimbatore; buses between Coimbatore, Tiruppur and Erode stop in the town. Tiruppur is the nearest railway station, and Coimbatore International Airport is the nearest airport.
